newsitem.title: USA: Clinton taps Pickering for under secretary of state.
newsitem.headline: Clinton taps Pickering for under secretary of state.

text.p: President Bill Clinton plans to nominate former U.S. ambassador to Russia Thomas Pickering as under secretary of state for political affairs, the third-ranking post at the State Department, the White House said on Friday.
In a separate statement, the White House said Clinton also planned to nominate Stuart Eizenstat to be under secretary of state for economics, business and agriculture.
Both positions require the approval of the U.S. Senate.
Pickering is one of the most experienced U.S. diplomats, having served as ambassador to Russia, India, Israel and Jordan as well as at the United Nations.
A U.S. official said Pickering would replace Peter Tarnoff, the current under secretary for political affairs, who will remain in the post until Pickering is confirmed by the Senate.

Pickering, a career diplomat, retired from the foreign service last year following a tour as ambassador to Russia and took a position with a private foundation that studies matters related to Russia and the former Soviet republics.

Eizenstat, currently the under secretary of commerce for international affairs, is a longtime public servant, having worked in the administrations of former Presidents Lyndon Johnson and Jimmy Carter.
From 1977 to 1981 Eizenstat served in the White House as Carter's chief domestic policy adviser.
